- When sentiment is strongly positive (e.g., >0.4) and forecast spikes upward, reduce the peak by 5–10% to avoid overshoot.  
- If sentiment is negative (e.g., < -0.3) and forecast is high, lower the forecast by 3–7% to reflect mean reversion.  
- If recent history shows a sharp upward trend followed by a drop, model tends to overcorrect — dampen the next forecast peak.  
- When sentiment is neutral or mixed, model often overestimates short-term volatility — use a 2–5% downward bias for 30-day horizon.  
- If sentiment history includes multiple large positive spikes, model tends to overreact — apply a smoothing filter to reduce forecast volatility.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome is consistently below forecast, apply a 3–6% downward adjustment to future predictions.  
- If sentiment is consistently positive but price is flat or declining, model overestimates momentum — reduce forecast by 2–5% for next period.
